claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you'd like me to check eligibility for? If so, could you tell me their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know you have an 8-year-old son, Alex.

Before I can properly assess your eligibility, I need to understand a bit more about your circumstances. Let me start with this question:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand the arrangements better.

**Who does Alex currently live with?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in local authority care - he's at a children's home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that important information. Before I can make my assessment, I need to check the specific rules around this situation. Let me review the guidance on Child Benefit for children in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. I've reviewed the guidance on children in care. I have one more important question to properly assess your situation:

**Does Alex spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you, or does he spend 2 nights in a row each week (or 7 days or more in a row) at home with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't come home to stay with me. He's at the children's home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the guidance I've reviewed:

**You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why: According to the UK government's Child Benefit rules, when a child is in local authority care for more than 8 weeks, you usually stop being entitled to Child Benefit. However, there is an exception if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home with you, or if they spend 2 nights in a row each week (or 7 days or more in a row) at home.

Since Alex is in full-time care at the children's home and does not spend any time at home with you, this exception does not apply. Therefore, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

However, I'd recommend contacting HMRC directly to discuss your specific circumstances, as they may be able to provide further guidance or clarification.
